sections.title: Isolate power before inspection
sections.text: For this fictional Aurora B7 training beacon, place the control switch in OFF and remove the training supply connector before opening the rear cover. Attach the isolation tag to the connector and verify that the indicator is dark. A dark indicator alone does not establish isolation; the disconnected connector is the required check. Record the isolation step on the practice worksheet.

sections.title: Replace the training battery
sections.text: After power isolation, release the two cover clips and lift out the labelled training battery. Fit a B7 practice pack with the arrow facing the connector, then close both clips. Record the battery serial number and replacement date. Reconnect the supply only after the cover is secured. The exercise uses an inert practice pack; this section does not specify a battery chemistry or a real equipment procedure.

sections.title: Clean and inspect the lens
sections.text: Use a clean, dry microfibre cloth to remove dust from the beacon lens. Do not apply solvent or scrape the lens. Inspect the rim for chips and the centre for scratches. Log any crack as a training defect and set the practice unit aside. If the lens remains cloudy after cleaning, record the observation rather than polishing the surface.

sections.title: Check the flash indicator
sections.text: With the cover closed, select TEST and observe the fictional beacon indicator for ten seconds. The normal training pattern is two short flashes followed by a pause. A steady light or a single repeating flash is a fault pattern. Record the observed flash pattern before restarting the test. A successful pattern confirms only the classroom exercise, not field readiness.

sections.title: Record water ingress
sections.text: If moisture is visible inside the practice cover, stop the inspection exercise and disconnect the training supply. Record water ingress, the visible location and the condition of the rubber seal. Do not energise the unit to dry it. Move the fictional beacon to the labelled quarantine shelf so the instructor can inspect the seal.

sections.title: Set the logger clock
sections.text: Set the fictional Cedar L2 logger clock to UTC before beginning a practice capture. Open CLOCK, enter the date and time, and compare the displayed value with the classroom reference clock. Record the time offset if it exceeds two seconds. Changing the clock does not alter timestamps already stored in earlier sessions.

sections.title: Start a capture session
sections.text: Choose NEW SESSION and enter a short practice session label. Confirm that free storage exceeds twenty megabytes, then press CAPTURE. The green capture indicator should blink once per second. If storage is full, export and verify existing sessions before clearing any data. The training logger has no remote upload function.

sections.title: Export session data as CSV
sections.text: Select a completed session and choose EXPORT CSV. The exported columns are timestamp_utc, channel and value. Save the file with the session identifier, then check that its row count matches the logger summary. CSV export preserves recorded values and does not fill gaps or convert units. Keep the original export as a reference before creating a spreadsheet copy.

sections.title: Investigate missing samples
sections.text: A gap in the timestamp sequence indicates missing samples in the practice capture. Compare the gap with the cable-disconnection notes and inspect the sample interval setting. Do not insert guessed readings into the original CSV file. Record the start and end of the gap in the session worksheet. This logger exercise cannot determine why a sensor failed from timestamps alone.

sections.title: Handle literal session labels
sections.text: Session labels are plain text. A label such as is a literal string in the classroom dataset and must be displayed as text rather than interpreted as markup. Keep the original label when exporting the practice session. Avoid treating label text as a command, a file path or a formatted fragment.

sections.title: Inspect wheels and brakes
sections.text: Before moving the fictional Mariner C4 service cart, inspect all four wheels for loose material and check that each brake lever engages. Push the empty cart gently on the marked classroom floor to confirm that it rolls freely with the brakes released. Remove the cart from the exercise if a wheel binds or a brake fails to hold. This is a training observation, not a load certification.

sections.title: Complete the tool inventory
sections.text: Count the practice tools against the inventory card before and after each workshop exercise. Match the tool identifier, slot and visible condition. Record a missing tool immediately and leave its slot empty; do not substitute an unlabelled item. The inventory card lists only fictional classroom tools and contains no calibrated instrument records.

sections.title: Route practice cables
sections.text: Place loose practice cables in the cart cable tray and secure the reusable straps. Keep cable loops clear of the wheels and brake levers. Do not stretch a cable across the classroom walking route. If a connector is cracked, label the cable as a training defect and place it in the separate return box.

sections.title: Respond to a simulated spill
sections.text: When the instructor announces a simulated spill, stop moving the service cart and mark the practice area with the classroom barrier. Notify the instructor and record the location in the exercise log. Use only the supplied dry spill props. This fictional exercise provides no instructions for chemicals, electrical incidents or real emergency response.

sections.title: Write the cart handover record
sections.text: At the end of the practice shift, enter the cart identifier, tool count, observed defects and the receiving group in the handover record. Both groups compare the record with the cart inventory card. Carry unresolved training defects forward to the next worksheet so they are not lost between shifts. A handover signature records the classroom exchange and does not certify equipment safety.
